rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains the hypocrites' habit: when meeting believers they profess faith to fend them off; this adds their mockery, guile, and situational motive rather than repeating the opening description.
rows.anchor: بيان لدأب المنافقين وأنهم إذا أستقبلوا المؤمنين دفعوهم عن أنفسهم بقولهم آمنا إستهزاء

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam distinguishes the first profession as beginning faith and this one as sincerity; al-Alusi rejects this because their verbal confession was already known and the proposed distinction lacks support.
rows.anchor: والقول بأن المراد ب ( آمنا ) أولا الأخبار عن إحداث الإيمان وهنا عز إحداث إخلاص الإيمان مما أرتضاه الإمام ولا أقتدي به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Liqāʾ means meeting someone face-to-face nearby and is one of fourteen verbal nouns of laqiya; Abū Ḥanīfa and Ibn al-Sumayqiʿ read lāqaw, which al-Baḥr treats as the simple verb.
rows.anchor: واللقاء إستقبال الشخص قريبا منه وهو أحد أربعة عشر مصدرا للقى وقرأ أبو حنيفة وإبن السميقع لاقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of 'we believe' is omitted either because the preceding passage specified belief in God and the Last Day or because it means belief in what the believers believe; the proposed Moses-only reading is remote.
rows.anchor: حذف المفعول في آمنا قيل إكتفاء بالتقييد قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No sound occasion-of-revelation report is known to al-Alusi; he rejects accounts passed through al-Suddī al-ṣaghīr, whom he calls a liar, and dismisses that chain as fabricated.
rows.anchor: ولم يصح عندي في سبب نزول هذه الآية شيء وأما ما ذكره الزمخشري والبيضاوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaliyā ilayhim means they were alone with their leaders; the omitted first object is understood, while ilā conveys moving away from one thing toward another. The phrase also recalls the idiom 'seek the matter, your blame is past'.
rows.anchor: من خلوت به وإليه إذا أنفردت معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading khalaw as 'they mocked them in private' is unsuitable: no trusted attestation gives khalā that explicit meaning, and the idiom about playing with someone's honor can retain its literal or 'gain power over' sense.
rows.anchor: وإحتمال أن يكون من خلوت به اي سخرت منه فمعنى الآية إذا أنهوا السخرية معهم

rows.speaker: النضر بن شميل
rows.claim: Al-Naḍr b. Shumayl claims ilā here means maʿa, 'with'; al-Alusi says there is no evidence for this or for treating the preposition as a substitute for biʾ.
rows.anchor: وزعم النضر بن شميل أن ( إلى ) هنا بمعنى مع ولا دليل عليه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib understands the root khalw as a place, space, or time being empty of an occupant; al-Alusi notes that taking it to mean 'pass away' is then figurative.
rows.anchor: ويفهم من كلام الراغب أن أصل معنى الخلو فراغ المكان والحيز عن شاغل وكذا الزمان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the hypocrites' 'satans' as the people who instructed them to deny the truth, identified here as Jews.
rows.anchor: من كانوا يأمرونهم بالتكذيب من اليهودكما قاله إبن عباس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and a group identify their satans as soothsayers, named for rebellion and for making evil seem good and good seem evil.
rows.anchor: أو كهنتهم كما قاله الضحاك وجماعة وسموا بذلك لتمردهم وتحسينهم القبيح

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī takes the satans to be jinn; al-Alusi says this interpretation does not occur to him as plausible.
rows.anchor: وحمله على شياطين الجن كما قاله الكلبي مما لا يختلج بقلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the referents are soothsayers, their jinn companions may explain the name; al-Alusi lists several soothsayers active in the Prophet's era, including Kaʿb b. al-Ashraf and Abū Burda.
rows.anchor: وكان على عهده صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كثير منهم ككعب بن الأشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shayāṭīn is a broken plural, though a rare anomalous reading treats it like a sound masculine plural, tanazzalat bihi al-shayāṭūn.
rows.anchor: والشياطين جمع تكسير وإجراؤه مجرى الصحيح كما في بعض الشواذ تنزلت به الشياطون

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basran derivation makes shayṭān a fayʿāl with a radical nūn, from shatana, 'to be far away,' because Satan is distant from obedience.
rows.anchor: والمفرد شيطان وهو فيعال عند البصريين فنونه أصلية من شطن أي بعد

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans derive shayṭān as faʿlān, with an added nūn, from shāṭa, meaning to perish, fail, or burn with anger.
rows.anchor: وعند الكوفيين وزنه فعلان فنونه زائدة من شاط يشيط إذا هلك أو بطل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās defines a shayṭān broadly as any rebel among jinn, humans, or animals.
rows.anchor: وروى عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن الشيطان كل متمرد من الجن والإنس والدواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their 'we are with you' denotes spiritual alliance: sharing their leaders' Judaism, described as the root of evils.
rows.anchor: قالوا إنا معكم أي معية معنوية وهي مسواتهم لهم في إعتقاد اليهودية وهو أم الخبائث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the contrast in form: a nonassertive verbal clause to believers feigning a new act of faith, but an emphatic nominal clause to leaders to claim lasting allegiance and forestall their doubts.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن الوجه هو الأول إذ يرد على الأخيرين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says they assert themselves with leaders because they sincerely wish to reassure them, whereas they withhold assertion when speaking to believers because they do not care about them.
rows.anchor: إن التأكيد كما يكون لأزالة الإنكار والشك يكون لصدق الرغبة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they avoid claiming full, settled faith before perceptive believers, while their leaders would accept such a claim; al-Alusi finds this and the desire-based account unpersuasive.
rows.anchor: أو لأنهم لو قالوا إنا مؤمنون كان إدعاء لكمال الإيمان وثباته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites may assert allegiance to leaders to claim eligibility for the believers' legal treatment and protection from conflict; they had already used an oath by God and the Last Day to deceive believers.
rows.anchor: إنهم للتقية والخداع ودعوى أنهم مثل المؤمنين في الإيمان

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read maʿakum with a vowel on ʿayn; a rare reading with sukūn is dialectal among Rabīʿa and Ghanm.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ( معكم ) بتحريك العين وقريء شاذا بسكونها وهي لغة ربيعة

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazālī defines mockery as contempt and pointing out defects in a laughable way, which may be done through mimicry, speech, gesture, or sign.
rows.anchor: وذكر حجة الإسلام الغزالي أن الإستهزاء الإستحقار والإستهانة والتنبيه على العيوب والنقائص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects al-Rāzī's definition of mockery as outwardly showing agreement while inwardly carrying its opposite, because it conflicts with language and common usage.
rows.anchor: وقول الرازي إنه عبارة عن إظهار موافقة مع إبطال ما يجري مجرى السوء على طريق السخرية غير موافق للغة والعرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The last clause may be a resumption answering the leaders' implied question about why the hypocrites associate with believers; alternatively it is a badal, confirmation, or explanation of the necessary implication of allegiance. The learned prefer resumption, though innamā makes an implied question less likely.
rows.anchor: وأولى الأوجه عند المحققين الإستئناف لولا ما ذكره الشيخ في دلائل الأعجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final word has rare readings that lighten the hamza or replace it with a yāʾ; some omit the yāʾ and give the zāy a ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( مستهزؤن ) بتخفيف الهمزة وبقلبها ياء مضمونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those referred to are the hypocrites described above: they claim rectitude while corrupting, call believers foolish while themselves foolish, and mock the mocked; the demonstrative marks their remoteness in evil.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى المنافقين الذين تقدم ذكرهم الجامعين للأوصاف الذميمة من دعوى الصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purchase explains how their shameful traits arose: they chose error, lost their bargain, and wandered from the straight path; the sentence can also summarize their condition, explain the mockery, or confirm their being left to stray.
rows.anchor: فإن السامع بعد سماع ذكرهم وإجراء تلك الأوصاف عليهم كأنه يسأل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative description restricts the predicate rhetorically to these hypocrites because they excel in the combined enormity of their traits, although other unbelievers share in error.
rows.anchor: وفيه حصر المسند على المسند إليه لكون تعريف الموصول للجنس بمنزلة تعيف اللام الجنسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguidance is deviation from the proper course and guidance is turning toward it; both also describe religious error and uprightness.
rows.anchor: والضلالة الجور عن القصد والهدى التوجه إليه ويطلقان على العدول عن الصواب في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the hypocrites did not possess guidance as a literal purchase price, ishtirāʾ can mean choosing error over guidance; alternatively, they exchanged their full capacity and supporting means for guidance, or their innate fitra.
rows.anchor: فأما أن يقال إن الإشتراء مجاز عن الأخيار لأن المشتري للشيء مختار له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the Mufti's objection that innate guidance is common to everyone: these hypocrites first lost it through their parents' Judaizing, then squandered it through hypocrisy despite signs, instruction, and direct counsel.
rows.anchor: إن الموصوفين بالنفاق المذكور هم الذين ضيعوا الفطرة أشد تضييع بتهويد الآباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor of purchasing is apt because they received overwhelming signs, miracles, admonition, and teaching that fully enabled guidance, but rejected them and fell into ruin.
rows.anchor: لكنهم نبذوا ذلك فوقعوا في مهاوي المهالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi takes the purchased guidance to mean their belief in Muḥammad's advent and truth, which they found in the Torah and invoked before his coming; he rejects identifying it with outward prayer, almsgiving, fasting, and warfare.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالهدى ما كانوا عليه من التصديق ببعثته

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes, including Mujāhid, understand 'those' as the hypocrites; al-Alusi endorses this because it follows the immediate context.
rows.anchor: هو الذي ذهب إليه أكثر المفسرين والمروي عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reportedly applies the verse's demonstrative to the People of the Book generally; al-Alusi considers this interpretation distant as the occasion of the verse.
rows.anchor: وروى عن قتادة أنهم أهل الكتاب مطلقا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd reportedly take the referents as all unbelievers; al-Alusi rejects these as the intended referents, though the wording may apply to them too.
rows.anchor: أن الآية بظاهر مفهومها تصدق على من أرادوا لا أن الآية نزلت فيهم

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر وابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Yaḥyā b. Yaʿmar and Ibn Isḥāq read the initial hamza of 'they purchased' with kasra as the original vowel when two sukūns meet.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن يعمر وإبن إسحاق ( أشتروا الضلالة ) بالكسر

rows.speaker: أبو السماك
rows.claim: Abū al-Sammāk reads the word with fatḥa by assimilation to the preceding vowel; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī incline the alif of hudā according to Tamīm usage.
rows.anchor: وأبو السماك ( أشتروا ) بالفتح إتباعا لما قبل وأمال حمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ coordinates the loss of profit with the purchase as part of the relative clause; it signals the immediate consequence of the transaction, and al-Alusi rejects parses that make the relative clause an independent subject or predicate.
rows.anchor: عطف على الصلة وأتى بالفاء للإشارة إلى تعقب نفي الربح للشراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse extends the trade metaphor: their lost guidance is capital and the missed benefits of guidance are profit, portraying their ruin as a merchant's worst loss.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية ترشيح لما سمعت من المجاز فيما قبلها والمقصد الأصلي تصوير خسارهم بفوت الفوائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing profit to the trade is metonymy for its owners; saying they did not profit implicitly condemns the loss and mocks their ignorance, while the following denial of guidance confirms actual loss rather than a neutral break-even result.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الربح إلى التجارة وهو لأربابها ماجز للملابسة وكنى في مقام الذم ينفي الربح عن الخسران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ordinary trade a person may neither profit nor lose, but religious commerce has only guidance or misguidance; the context 'they were not guided' therefore marks the loss unmistakably.
rows.anchor: والربح والخسران في الدين لا واسطة بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause 'they were not guided' most naturally coordinates with 'their trade did not profit'; it completes the implied loss and acts as rhetorical completion or intensification rather than needless repetition.
rows.anchor: عطف على ما ربحت للقرب مع التناسب والتفرع بإعتبار المعنى الكنائي

rows.speaker: الشريف
rows.claim: Al-Sharīf prefers attaching 'they were not guided' to the earlier 'they purchased misguidance'; al-Alusi objects that this order is confusing and that the meanings are too close for a good conjunction.
rows.anchor: وقال الشريف قدس سره : إن العطف

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads 'their trades' in the plural because each hypocrite has a trade; the majority's singular indicates that their many transactions form one common market.
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبن أبي عبلة تجاراتهم على الجمع ووجهه أن لكل واحد تجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poetic line uses ishtāla for shāla yashūlu, showing an iftiʿāl form functioning like the simple verb.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا أشتال سهيل في السحر كشعلة القابس ترمي بالشرر فأفتعل فيه بمعنى فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause may be accusative by syntactic attachment or by detachment for condemnation, or nominative as a new subject whose predicate is 'those are the losers'; this last reading makes the statement nearly parenthetical.
rows.anchor: يحتمل النصب والرفع والأول إما على الإتباع أو القطع أي أذم والثاني إما على الثاني

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the covenant metaphor by the conventional image of a cord, representing the stable connection between two parties.
rows.anchor: كما قال الزمخشري من حيث تسميتهم العهد بالحبل على سبيل الإستعارة لما فيه من ثبات الوصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi analyzes naqd as a vivid explicit metaphor for undoing an organized body, made apt by the implicit comparison of the covenant to a cord; this shows implicit metaphor can occur without an imagined image.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أن في الآية استعارة بالكناية والنقض استعارة تحقيقية تصريحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the covenant the rational evidence God established through human nature, the cosmos, prophets, and scripture; on this reading its breakers are all unbelievers.
rows.anchor: إما العهد المأخوذ بالعقل وهو الحجة القائمة على عباده تعالى الدالة على وجوده ووحدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is the pledge conveyed by messengers: when a messenger comes with miracles they must affirm and follow him, as earlier scriptures mention; breakers are then the People of the Book and their hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وأما المأخوذ من جهة الرسل على الأمم بأنهم إذا بعث إليهم رسول مصدق بالمعجزات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reported meanings are the trust borne by humanity after the heavens and earth declined it, or Israel's pledges not to shed blood or expel one another; these reflect different proposed occasions of revelation.
rows.anchor: وقيل الأمانة التي حملها الإنسان بعد إباء السموات والأرض عن أن يحملنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the general meaning of God's covenant because the wording gives no decisive basis for restricting it; views about its particular referents rest on differing revelation-context reports.
rows.anchor: والظاهر العموم و ﴿ من ﴾ للإبتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is primarily spatial or temporal departure after the covenant was confirmed, implying they broke it immediately after securing it; treating it as an empty connective is remote. Mīthāq is what confirmed the covenant, a source according to some and a noun according to others.
rows.anchor: وتدل على أن النقض حصل عقيب توثق العهد من غير فصل

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows mīthāq to be a verbal noun meaning confirmation; its pronoun may refer to God's covenant or to the covenant itself, making the source annexed to agent or object respectively.
rows.anchor: وأفهم كلام أبي البقاء أن الميثاق هنا مصدر بمعنى التوثقة وفي الضمير الإحتمالان

rows.speaker: الساليكوتي
rows.claim: Al-Sālikūtī rejects taking the pronoun in 'its confirmation' back to God, since the meaning depends on reference to the covenant and a return to a possessed noun is disfavored; al-Alusi notes that such reference is common in verbal genitives.
rows.anchor: ولم يجوزه الساليكوتي لأن المعنى لا يتم بدون اعتبار العهد فهو أهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains what they sever as the Messenger, whom they cut off through denial and disobedience.
rows.anchor: الأول رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قطعوه بالتكذيب والعصيان قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations of what God commanded to be joined are the revealed word left unpracticed, affirmation of all prophets rather than some, or kinship ties; Qatāda gives the kinship interpretation.
rows.anchor: الثاني القول فإنه تعالى أمر أن يوصل بالعمل فلم يصلوه ولم يعملوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers a comprehensive reading: whatever causes the intended bond between God and servant is covered, giving the phrase its full general scope without unsupported restriction.
rows.anchor: الخامس الأمر الشامل لما ذكر مما يوجب قطعه قطع الوصلة بين الله تعالى وبين العبد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some prefer kinship ties because they see the verse progressing from violation of God's right to violation of people's rights; al-Alusi finds this argument weak.
rows.anchor: ورجح بعضهم ما قبله بأن الظاهر أن هذا توصيف للفاسقين بأنهم يضيعون حق الخلق

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites define a command as a verbal request for an act issued from a position of superiority; Abū al-Ḥusayn instead says the speaker must claim superiority, a definition challenged by Pharaoh's quoted request.
rows.anchor: والأمر القول الطالب للفعل مع علو عند المعتزلة أو استعلاء عند أبي الحسين

rows.speaker: الفقهاء
rows.claim: Jurists treat amr as shared between speech and action, citing the description of Pharaoh's command as not rightly guided.
rows.anchor: وذهب الفقهاء إلى أن الأمر مشترك بين القول والفعل لأنه يطلق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause 'that it be joined' is best taken as a genitive or accusative apposition to the pronoun in 'what God commanded,' because that makes severing what was ordered joined more forceful; other parsing proposals are rejected.
rows.anchor: يحتمل النصب والخفض على أنه بدل من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their corruption includes committing sins whose harm spreads, which is preferable to narrower readings of recruiting others into unbelief or intimidating routes to block migration; 'on earth' emphasizes harm beyond themselves.
rows.anchor: أو بأنهم يرتكبون كل معصية يتعدى ضررها ويطير في الآفاق شررها ولعل هذا أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to the fāsiqūn through their detailed traits and signals their great distance in blame; exclusive 'losers' describes their complete loss of reason, eternal life, reward, capital, and profit, extending the preceding trade metaphor.
rows.anchor: حصر الخاسرين عليهم باعتبار كمالهم في الخسران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham is praised for perfecting others after his own perfection; tawṣiya is urging another toward a beneficial religious act by speech or sign, before death or at another time, and its root connotes joining.
rows.anchor: مدح له عليه السلام بتكميله غيره إثر مدحه بكماله في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'with it' most likely refers to the community/religion, since that antecedent is explicit and Jacob's coordination begins a new account of prophets transmitting the true religion; taking it as 'I submitted' has proximity and wording in its favor.
rows.anchor: ويرجح الأول كون المرجع مذكورا صريحا وكذا ترك المضمر إلى المظهر

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read awṣā, with no necessary implication of greater frequency than the form waṣṣā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وإبن عامرأوصى ولا دلالة فيها على التكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb is coordinated with Abraham and is read nominative as a new subject with an omitted predicate meaning 'likewise'; a reading in the accusative coordinates him with Abraham's sons, while making him the implicit agent is remote.
rows.anchor: ويعقوب عطف على إبراهيم ورفعه على الإبتداء وحذف الخبر أي يعقوب كذلك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says Jacob was named because Esau emerged first and Jacob followed holding his heel; al-Alusi doubts its authenticity.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمى يعقوب لأنه وعيصا كانا توأمين فتقدم عيص وخرج يعقوب على أثره آخذا بعقبه

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: Basrans posit an omitted verb of saying before 'O my sons'; it is singular if Jacob is read accusative and dual if he is nominative. Kufans need no ellipsis because testament itself entails speech.
rows.anchor: يابني على إضمار القول عند البصريين ويقدر بصيغة الأفراد على تقدير نصب يعقوب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads 'an yā banī'; this removes the need for an implicit saying verb for Basrans, and some authorities indicate that adding one is then impermissible.
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه : أن يا بني ولا حاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Itqān lists twelve sons of Abraham and twelve of Jacob, naming each group, as historical context for the address to their descendants.
rows.anchor: وبنو إبراهيم على ما في الإتقان إثنا عشر وهم إسماعيل وإسحق ومدين وزمزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God selected and enabled them for Islam, the religion that is inherently the purest; the wording does not mean Islam is pure only for them, and the term can denote earlier true religion despite later customary restriction.
rows.anchor: إن الله أصطفى لكم الدين أي جعل لكم الدين الذي هو صفوة الأديان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Do not die except as Muslims' forbids being in a non-Muslim state at death; although death itself is outside human control, maintaining the state that determines one's death is actionable. The command means remain steadfast in Islam.
rows.anchor: نهى عن الإتصاف بخلاف حال الإسلام وقت الموت والمفهوم من الآية فظاهرا النهي عن الموت

rows.speaker: الفاضل اليمني
rows.claim: Al-Fāḍil al-Yamanī calls the construction a metaphorical negation of the person to negate a particular state; al-Alusi says negating a person could only negate all attributes, not one state.
rows.anchor: وقال الفاضل اليمني : إن هذا كناية بنفي الذات عن نفي الحال

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the required Islam is inward faith alone because bodily deeds are hardly possible at death, and cite a Prophetic supplication asking that the living be kept Muslim and the dead die in faith; al-Alusi finds this unpersuasive.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن الإسلام المأمور به هنا ما يكون بالقلب دون العمل بالجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī reports that the verse was revealed in response to Jews who told the Prophet that Jacob had instructed his sons to be Jews; this occasion supports addressing Jews of his time.
rows.anchor: فقد ذكر الواحدي أن الآية نزلت في اليهودي حين قالوا للنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Jewish addressees, disconnected am means 'rather' plus a rebuking question: they were absent from Jacob's deathbed and cannot assert what they claim; it may instead ask whether their ancestors witnessed his Islamic testament.
rows.anchor: إما منقطعة بمعنى بل وهمزة الإنكار ومعنى بل الإضراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A connected am can contrast the known absence with the impossible claim of witnessing, binding the addressees either way: if absent, they invent the report; if present, they contradict the known account.
rows.anchor: وإما متصلة وفي الكلام حذفوالتقدير أكنتم غائبين

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that no one is known to permit deleting the clause before connected am; he says deletion is only attested for am with its coordinate.
rows.anchor: وأعترض أبو حيان على هذا الوجه بأنا لا نعلم أحدا أجاز حذف الجملة المعطوف عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view addresses believers: the report of earlier prophets' circumstances without hearing or reading is a prophetic sign and a reason to follow the Messenger; its proponent sets aside the weak revelation occasion.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب للمؤمنين ومعنى بل الإضراب عن الكلام الأول

rows.speaker: السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyūṭī says he could not find the stated occasion of revelation, a reservation al-Alusi links to the weakness of the believers-address interpretation's disregard of it.
rows.anchor: حتى قال الإمام السيوطي : لم أقف عليه والشهداءجمع شهيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuhadāʾ can mean witnesses or those present; ḥaḍara is read with a kasra in an unusual dialect or by overlap of two patterns.
rows.anchor: والشهداءجمع شهيد أو شاهد بمعنى حاضر وحضر من باب قعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'When he said to his sons' is an apposition of inclusion to 'when death came to Jacob,' since both events are intended and the second supplies detail; attaching the first temporal clause to 'they said' breaks the sense.
rows.anchor: إذ قال لبنيه بدل من ( إذ حضر ) بدل اشتمال وكلاهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 'what will you worship after me,' mā is nominative with an omitted resumptive pronoun; treating it as an object loses the question's fitting gradation from asking what a thing is to identifying who it is.
rows.anchor: ما تعبدون من بعدي أي أي شيء تعبدونه بعد موتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's question is not genuine inquiry but a way to urge continued monotheism and Islam and renew their pledge; he reportedly saw fire worship in Egypt and feared for his sons.
rows.anchor: وفي السؤال عن حالهم بعد موته دليل على أن الغرض حثهم على ما كانوا عليه حال حياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons' answer is a new sentence responding to the implied question; attributing the deity to several forefathers stresses their shared belief, and Ishmael is named before Isaac because he was older.
rows.anchor: إستئناف وقع جوابا لسؤال نشأ عن حكاية السؤال وفي إضافة الإله إلى المتعدد إشارة إلى الإتفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob calls his uncle Ishmael a father either by letting the majority outweigh one exception or because uncles and fathers are joined like brothers; a Prophetic report in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs says an uncle is his father's counterpart.
rows.anchor: وعده من آباء يعقوب مع أنه عمه تغليا للأكثر على الأقل أو لأنه شبه العم بالأب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report cited from Ibn Abī Shayba has the Prophet ask that his family honor al-ʿAbbās, since he is the remainder of his forefathers, illustrating broad use of 'fathers.'
rows.anchor: والآية على حد ما أخرجه إبن أبي شيبة وغيره من قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads 'abīkum' in the singular, with Ishmael and Isaac coordinated as an appositional clarification; alternatively it may be a plural with the nūn omitted in annexation, as in cited poetry.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسنأبيكوهو إما مفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'One God' is an appositional clarification of 'the god of your fathers,' removing any inference of multiple gods; grammarians differ on whether an indefinite apposition must be described.
rows.anchor: والنكرة تبدل من المعرفة بشرط ان توصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'We submit to Him' means yielding and affirming servitude, obeying His commands and prohibitions in word and belief, or entering and remaining in Islam; it may be circumstantial or parenthetical.
rows.anchor: أي مذعنون مقرون بالعبودية وقيل : خاضعون منقادون مستسلمون

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers coordinating 'we submit' with 'we worship,' making the sons give two answers to Jacob's question and thus an enhanced response.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : الأبلغ أن تكون معطوفة على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they concealed truth for low worldly motives, they exchanged guidance for error in this life and forgiveness for punishment in the next; this explains the severe threat against concealers.
rows.anchor: بسبب كتمانهم الحق للمطامع الدنية والأغراض الدنيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purchase sentence can stand independently as the answer to why the threat is so severe, or be a second predicate: the first describes threat severity and the second the ugliness of concealment.
rows.anchor: والجملة إما مستأنفة فإنه لما عظم وعيد الكاتمين كان مظنة أن يسأل عن سبب عظم وعيدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'How patient they are with the Fire!' is a sarcastic wonder for believers at their heedless commission of acts that incur Hell; they are not truly patient.
rows.anchor: أي ما أشد صبرهم وهو تعجب للمؤمنين من إرتكابهم موجباتها من غير مبالاة وإلا فأي صبر لهم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most grammarians take mā in the exclamation as a complete indefinite noun in the nominative; al-Farrāʾ treats it as interrogative carrying an exclamatory sense, while al-Akhfash reports relative and indefinite-adjectival analyses.
rows.anchor: في مثل هذا التركيب قيل : نكرة تامة وعليه الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barazū means Ṭālūt and his company emerged into an open, level stretch of land opposite Goliath and his troops for combat.
rows.anchor: أي ظهر طالوت ومن معه وصاروا في براز من الأرض وهو ما أنكشف منها وأستوى لجالوت وجنوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole army prayed after the weak-hearted had gained courage, humbly turning to God and disavowing their own power.
rows.anchor: بعد أن قويت قلوب الضعفاء متضرعين إلى الله تعالى متبرئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking God to pour patience means to grant and enable self-restraint in battle; asking to stabilize their feet means complete strength and steadfastness in confrontation, not merely keeping their feet in one spot.
rows.anchor: أي صب ذلك علينا ووفقنا له والمراد به حبس النفس للقتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for aid through the enemy's defeat and rout; calling Goliath's force 'the unbelieving people' instead of using a pronoun states the reason they deserve victory.
rows.anchor: أي أعنا عليهم بقهرهم وهزمهم ووضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer invokes God's nurturing lordship, pictures abundant patience poured like water to cool their hearts and replace withheld water, makes them vessels through ʿalā, and magnifies patience with an indefinite noun.
rows.anchor: فيه التوسل بوصف الربوبية المنبئة عن التبليغ إلى الكمال وأما ثانيا فلأن فيه الإفراغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence is apt: patience at encounter, steadfast strength against the enemy, then victory; patience alone may lack resistance, and courage without victory yields no benefit.
rows.anchor: حيث طلبوا أولا إفراغ الصبر على قلوبهم عند اللقاء وثانيا ثبات القدم والقوة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says patience is the foundation, stability follows from it, and victory is the ultimate aim; though this seems to call for fāʾ, the reply says wāw better relies on the mind's natural ordering, as al-Sakkākī notes.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنما طلبوا أولا إفراغ الصبر لأنه ملاك الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After directing that an insolvent debtor be given time, the passage sets out how to document deferred rights and debt contracts.
rows.anchor: ولما أمر سبحانه بإنظار المعسر وتأجيله عقبه ببيان أحكتم الحقوق المؤجلة وعقود المداينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadāyantum means dealing with one another; adding bi-dayn makes explicit that the shared transaction is a debt, since the verb can also mean reciprocal recompense. Al-Alusi rejects reliance on context alone for legal clarity.
rows.anchor: فائدة ذكره تخليص المشترك ودفع الإيهام نصا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say dayn is mentioned to provide an explicit antecedent for the later pronoun; others say it improves the wording, but the objection that tadāyantum already supplies the sense is answered because it does not clearly identify the debt itself.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ذكر ليرجع اليه الضمير إذ لولاه لقيل : فاكتبوا الدين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view says the indefinite debt denotes debt generally and allows its division into current and deferred kinds; without the word, one might think debt is always deferred.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ذكر لأنه أبين لتنويع الدين إلى مؤجل وحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A specified term is a known time expressed in days, months, or comparable units; a harvest date is too uncertain and would undermine the agreement.
rows.anchor: بالأيام أو الأشهر أو نظائرهما مما يفيد العلم ويرفع الجهالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing the debt with its due date is more convenient and secure; most treat the instruction as recommended in view of the later trust exception.
rows.anchor: أي الدين بأجله لانه أرفق وأوثق والجمهور على استجابة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās restricts the debt here to forward-sale debt, reporting that God set and permitted such a deferred transaction before reciting the verse.
rows.anchor: فقد أخرج البخارى عنه أنه قال : أشهد أن السلف المضمون إلى أجل مسمى

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Imām Mālik uses the verse as evidence that a loan may have a deferred repayment date.
rows.anchor: واستدل الإمام مالك بها على جواز تأجيل القرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to have a just scribe specifies how to write and who does it; keeping either contracting party from writing prevents suspicion, and the scribe should be learned in law as well as fair and trustworthy.
rows.anchor: بيان لكيفية الكتابة المأمور بها وتعيين من يتولاها إثر الأمر بها إجمالا

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭībī sees a stated meaning plus an embedded implication: the writer must be legally knowledgeable to balance consequential matters; some infer that rulers should bar unqualified people from drafting legal documents.
rows.anchor: كما قال الطيبي مسوق لمعنى ومدمج فيه آخر بإشارة النص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The writer must not refuse to document the debt; 'as God taught him' means because God taught and favored him with documentary skill, like the command to do good as God did good to you.
rows.anchor: أي لأجل ما علمه الله تعالى من كتابه الوثائق وتفضل به عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'as God taught him' may modify the act of writing as an adverbial or circumstantial phrase, or attach to 'let him write'; the fāʾ can still connect because it functions semantically as a relative clause.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق الكاف بأن يكتب على أنه نعت لمصدر محذوف أو حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the second command repeats the earlier writing order, it emphasizes it because forbidding refusal does not explicitly command its opposite; some infer a communal obligation, but al-Alusi says this reading would impose hardship on the believers.
rows.anchor: والأمر بالكتابة بعد النهى عن الأداء منها على الأول للتأكيد وإحتيج إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On another parsing, the command requires writing in the taught, just manner after forbidding refusal of writing generally; this is not a repetition. Al-Alusi rejects the claim that repetition must follow, calling the distinction arbitrary when unrestricted and restricted commands concern one event.
rows.anchor: وأما على الوجه الثانى فلا تأكيد وإنما هو أمر بالكتابة المقيدة بعد النهي عن الإمتناع من المطلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mā in 'as God taught him' may be a verbal noun, particle of emphasis, relative pronoun, or adjective; pronoun reference changes accordingly, and some supply 'document writing' as the second object of 'taught.'
rows.anchor: قيل : إما مصدرية أو كافة وجوز أن تكون موصولة أو موصوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imlāl means dictating to a scribe; the form alternates with imlāʾ through sound changes involving the doubled consonant and final hamza.
rows.anchor: من الإملال بمعنى الإلقاء على الكاتب ما يكتبه وفعله أمللت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person owing the debt must dictate because that person is the one against whom a claim is made and must acknowledge it; attaching the command to that description implies a restriction to the debtor.
rows.anchor: وهو المطلوب لأنه المشهود عليه فلا بد أن يكون هو المقر لا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pairing God's majestic name with 'his Lord' combines majesty and gracious care to intensify the debtor's admonition to fear God.
rows.anchor: جمع بين الإسم الجليل والوصف الجميل مبالغة في الحث على التقوى

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: The prohibition on reducing any part of the dictated debt, even a small amount, is the transmitted interpretation from Saʿīd b. Jubayr; variant readings omit or double the hamza in shayʾan.
rows.anchor: وإن كان حقيرا وقرئ شيا بطرح الهمزة وشيا بالتشديد وهذا هو التفسير المأثور عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some refer 'let him fear' to the scribe, but al-Alusi rejects this: the debtor is particularly liable to reduce the amount, whereas the scribe might add or subtract, and fairness already governs the scribe.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يجوز أن يرجع ضمير يتق للكاتب وليس بشئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debtor receives both a positive command to fear God and a prohibition on reducing the debt because self-interest naturally drives people to repel harm from themselves.
rows.anchor: وإنما شدد في تكليف المملى حيث جمع فيه بين الأمر بالإتقاء والنهي عن البخس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Minhu can attach directly to 'reduce,' with min marking origin, or be a fronted circumstantial phrase; shayʾan can be its object or a cognate accusative.
rows.anchor: وجهان : أحدهما أن يكون متعلقا بيبخس و من لإبتداء الغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about an incapable debtor restates the topic for clarity; 'foolish' can mean incompetent or foolish (Ibn Zayd), unable to dictate (Mujāhid), or wasteful and religiously corrupt (al-Shāfiʿī).
rows.anchor: قاله ابن زيد أو جاهلا بالإملال قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Weak' means a child or senile elder; inability to dictate may be muteness, as reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, or any impediment including unfamiliarity with the language.
rows.anchor: أي صبيا أو شيخا خرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun hu either emphasizes inability to dictate personally, excluding figurative attribution, or serves as the subject with changed syntax to stress negation; his guardian then dictates fairly.
rows.anchor: والضمير البارز توكيد للضمير المستتر في أن يمل وفائدة التوكيد به رفع المجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The representative is whoever manages the incapable person's affairs, not only a formal guardian: the term includes a curator, agent, and translator; admitting for another here is valid, unlike admitting against another.
rows.anchor: أي متولي أمره وإن لم يكن خصوص الولي الشرعي فيشمل القيم والوكيل والمترجم

rows.speaker: ابن الفرس
rows.claim: Ibn al-Faras infers that guardians may not be unbelievers or sinners but may be enslaved or women because the verse requires only justice; al-Alusi dismisses this inference.
rows.anchor: ذكره ابن الفرس وليس بشيء كما لا يخفى

rows.speaker: الشعبي والجبائي والرماني
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī, al-Jubbāʾī, and al-Rummānī infer from 'let him write' and 'let no scribe refuse' that writing is a communal obligation; al-Ḥasan's position inclines that way.
rows.anchor: وإلى ذلك ذهب الشعبي والجبائي والرماني إلا أنهم قالوا : إنها واجبة على الكفاية

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the individual scribe must write when asked; another position recommends writing, and a report from al-Ḍaḥḥāk says its original obligation was later abrogated.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والضحاك : واجب عليه أن يكتب إذا أمر وقيل : هي مندوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istashhidū means request two people to bear witness to the transaction; alternatively its extra sīn and tāʾ may be redundant and mean simply 'witness.' The intensive noun suggests experienced, capable witnesses and may hint at recognized reliability.
rows.anchor: أي إطلبوهما ليتحملا الشهادة على ما جرى بينكما وجوز أن تكون السين والتاء زائدتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seek witnesses is considered recommended or obligatory according to the broader disagreement over these commands.
rows.anchor: والأمر للندب أو للوجوب على الخلاف في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression 'from your men' is linked to the command or describes the witnesses partitivally; its address to believers is taken to imply Muslim, adult, male, and free witnesses, based on the customary sense of complete men.
rows.anchor: وفي ذكر الرجال مضافا إلى ضمير المخاطبين دلالة على إشتراط الإسلام والبلوغ والذكورة

rows.speaker: الإمامية
rows.claim: The Imāmīs, along with Shurayḥ, Ibn Sīrīn, Abū Thawr, and ʿUthmān al-Battī, do not require a witness to be free, provided he is Muslim and upright; this differs from the report that ʿAlī rejected slave testimony entirely.
rows.anchor: وذهب الإمامية إلى عدم إشتراط الحرية في قبول الشهادة وإنما الشرط فيه عندهم الإسلام و العدالة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The verse does not address unbelievers testifying among themselves, but Abū Ḥanīfa allows this by analogy even when their religious communities differ.
rows.anchor: ولم تتعرض الآية لشهادة الكفار بعضهم على بعض وأجاز ذلك قياسا الإمام أبو حنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'If the two are not men' means the parties do not intend to summon two men, even if two are available; it negates the combined case rather than universally negating men, or the replacement clause would fail.
rows.anchor: أي لم يقصد إشهادهما ولو كانا موجودين والحكم من قبيل نفي العموم لا عموم النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If two men are not sought, the alternatives can be parsed elliptically as one man and two women testifying, serving as witnesses, or being requested as witnesses.
rows.anchor: أي فإن لم يكونا رجلين مجتمعين فليشهد رجل وإمرأتان أو فرجل وإمرأتان يشهدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man and two women suffice in testimony outside ḥudūd and qiṣāṣ according to al-Alusi's school, while al-Shāfiʿī confines it to property cases and excludes matters such as marriage.
rows.anchor: وكفاية الرجل والمرأتين في الشهادة فيما عدا الحدود والقصاص عندنا وعند الشافعى في الأموال خاصة

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik excludes such testimony from ḥudūd, qiṣāṣ, clientage, and proof of chastity, but accepts it for agency and wills where emancipation is not involved; women alone may testify in matters such as birth or virginity.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك : لا تجوز شهادة أولئك فدى الحدود ولا القصاص ولا الولاء ولا الإحصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rare reading gives the initial hamza of imraʾatān sukūn, apparently to avoid a sequence of moving consonants.
rows.anchor: وقرئ وإمرأتان بهمزة ساكنة ولعل ذلك لإجتماع المتحركات

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: The phrase 'from those you approve' can modify the male-and-female pair, the two male witnesses, or all solicited witnesses; Abū Ḥayyān attaches it to 'seek witnesses,' which al-Alusi says awkwardly separates the women's provision from its rationale.
rows.anchor: وإختار أو حيان تعلقه بإستشهدوا ليكون قيدا في الجميع ويلزمه الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names people whose outward reliability you approve, rather than implying access to their inward state; God judges the hidden reality. 'Among the witnesses' is a circumstantial phrase, with women included in the masculine plural by convention.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل من المرضيين لإفهامه إشتراط كونهم كذلك في نفس الأمر و لا طريق لنا إلى معرفته
